carbon_dioxide.summary: Indoor CO₂ levels indicate ventilation quality. Values above 1000 ppm signal poor ventilation; above 2000 ppm the air quality is considered unhealthy.

lines.description: Poor ventilation — consider opening a window or increasing airflow.
Unhealthy air quality — ventilate the space immediately.

humidity.source: WHO Housing and Health Guidelines (2018), ASHRAE Standard 55
humidity.summary: Comfortable indoor relative humidity is 40–60%. Below 40% the air becomes too dry (irritates mucous membranes). Above 60–70% mold and dust mites proliferate.

lines.description: Lower comfort boundary — below this the air may feel too dry.
Upper comfort boundary — above this condensation and mold risk increase.
Significant mold and dust-mite risk — take action to reduce humidity.

temperature.summary: Comfortable indoor temperature for living spaces is 18–26°C. Below 18°C is associated with increased respiratory illness risk (WHO minimum). Above 26°C thermal comfort drops significantly.

lines.description: WHO minimum for heated living spaces — prolonged exposure below this increases health risk.
Upper comfort limit — above this thermal comfort decreases and cooling is recommended.

pm25.summary: PM2.5 (fine particulate matter) penetrates deep into the lungs and affects cardiovascular and respiratory health. WHO 2021 guidelines are significantly stricter than previous versions.

lines.description: WHO 2021 24-hour mean guideline — sustained exposure above this increases health risk.
Poor air quality — run air purifier at higher setting and limit time indoors.

voltage.source: EN 50160 (Voltage Characteristics of Electricity Supplied by Public Distribution Networks)
voltage.summary: EU nominal supply voltage is 230V. EN 50160 allows ±10% (207–253V) under normal conditions. Sustained deviations outside this range may damage appliances and void warranties.

lines.description: EU lower limit (230V − 10%) — below this appliances may malfunction or be damaged.
EU upper limit (230V + 10%) — above this risk of appliance damage increases.

frequency.source: EN 50160 (Voltage Characteristics of Electricity Supplied by Public Distribution Networks)
frequency.summary: EU grid nominal frequency is 50 Hz. EN 50160 allows ±1% (49.5–50.5 Hz) for 99.5% of the year. Deviations affect motor-driven appliances and synchronised clocks.

lines.description: EU lower frequency limit — deviations indicate grid instability.
EU upper frequency limit — deviations indicate grid instability.

pressure.source: WMO — Guide to Meteorological Instruments and Methods of Observation
pressure.summary: Atmospheric pressure at sea level averages 1013.25 hPa. Normal range is roughly 950–1050 hPa depending on altitude and weather conditions. Low pressure (below ~1000 hPa) typically indicates stormy weather; high pressure (above ~1020 hPa) indicates fair weather. Note: if your sensor reads values far outside this range it may need calibration, or the unit may be Pa instead of hPa (divide by 100 to convert).

lines.description: Low pressure — below this, unsettled or stormy weather is likely.
High pressure — above this, fair and stable weather is likely.
